sections.overview: How to Treat Takayasu Arteritis in Ayurveda?
sections.introduction_of_the_disease: Takayasu Arteritis is a rare and treatable disease affecting one in 200000 people, of the age group 15 to 40 years. The patients of this disease are almost females. It is a combination of syndromes causing inflammation in blood vessels, also known as Vasculitis. This inflammation damages Aorta, the artery responsible for carrying blood from heart to various body parts and its main branches. The damage may lead to blockage, swelling, tearing, thickening, narrowing or bulging, etc. of artery walls resulting in the improper blood flow. The sufferers of this disorder can be found worldwide, but is more common in Asian countries. It may be hereditary sometimes. It results in absence of pulses in most of the cases, therefore, also known as Pulse-less disease by the professionals. The other clinical names are Occlusive thromboaortopathy, aortic arch syndrome, nonspecific aorto arteritis and Martorell syndrome.
sections.causes_of_takayasu_arteritis:
The exact cause of Takayasu is not clearly explained till the time, still some of them that have been seen in the patients are: 

 Autoimmune diseases – These are the health problems in which the immune system within the body attacks its own arteries mistakenly. 
 Virus or other infections – Any virus or other infections that occur time to time due to seasonal or environmental changes may trigger the problem.
sections.symptoms_of_takayasu_arteritis:
The symptoms of Takayasu Arteritis are often visible in two stages. The signs and symptoms at stage 1 may not be felt by everyone, not even diagnosed by the doctors and they become more severe, when reaches to stage 2. The main symptoms on both the stages are provided below: 
 Stage 1 or Systematic Phase 

 Fatigue 
 Abnormal Weight Loss 
 Muscle and Joint Pains 
 Mild fever accompanying Night Sweats 
 Abdominal Pain 
 Headaches 
 Chest Pain 
 Loss of Appetite 

 Stage 2 or Occlusive Phase 

 Arm or Chest Pain 
 High Blood Pressure 
 Heart stroke 
 Inflammation in Arteries 
 Infection 
 Weakness or pain in limbs 
 Dizziness 
 Visual and Speech changes 
 Disturbed memory 
 Breathlessness 
 Diarrhoea or blood in stools 
 Anemia 
 Hard and narrow blood vessels 
 Heart Failure 

 These symptoms are also unstable and vary with the time. For a proper treatment, a sharp eye has to be kept on these changing symptoms in the body in order to get it treated properly.
sections.risk_of_pregnancy: As the risk factor of the disease is the females below 40 years, they may face complications in their pregnancy. A normal and healthy pregnancy is possible living with this ill health, but only with some precautions. If a woman has Takayasu Arteritis, she should consult a doctor before conceiving baby and also during the pregnancy, so that the complications can be controlled at earlier stage. The allopathic medications for the disorder can also affect pregnancy as well as fertility of a woman but here you provided are the best herbal remedies for the treatment of this disorder without any side effect. It neither affects the fertility of a female nor triggers the pregnancy.
sections.diagnosis_of_takayasu_arteritis:
TAK can be easily diagnosed by the following ways: 

 Physical Exam / Pulse Check 
 Blood Test (ESR/CRP) 
 Imaging (MRA/CTA)
